newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rebels threaten to kill Japan diplomat.
newsitem.headline: Rebels threaten to kill Japan diplomat.

text.p: Peruvian rebels threatened to kill one of the Japanese diplomats taken hostage unless President Alberto Fujimori goes to the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima for negotiations, a Japanese Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Thursday.
The rebels made the threat in a telephone interview with the Lima radio station Radioprogramas on Wednesday, Foreign Ministry spokesman Ken Shimanouchi told a news conference.
"We confirmed with the local embassy that such demands had been made over the local radio," Shimanouchi said.
The guerrillas have threatened to kill all the hostages and the spokesman did not say if the diplomat had been singled out or if he might be the first victim.
The Japanese government was in the process of collecting more information and checking what the Peruvian government intended to do, he said.
Of the some 120 Japanese hostages, 15 are embassy staff, including ambassador to Peru Morihisa Aoki.
Shimanouchi also said that there have been no major developments in the past several hours.

The Cuban-inspired Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels, who stormed the residence on Tuesday during a reception held in honour of the Japanese emperor, are demanding the release of up to 500 jailed comrades.
While estimates by the government and released hostages put the number of captives between 200 and 300, a letter signed by the captives and faxed to relatives said the rebels were holding 490 men.
Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda was expected to leave Tokyo around midday for Lima to help in trying to resolve the crisis.
